Bubonic plague is transmitted by an inse.why: Rarely stated in this form. People name the flea, not its class: 'plague is transmitted by insects' has no exact hit, and 'bubonic plague' near 'insect' (2.5% of its mentions) samples as insect-repellent and pest-control copy, not the fact. 'Bubonic plague' near 'fleas' is 17.6%. It follows from plague being flea-borne and fleas being insects.

notes: Derived edit replacing the scouting's gharial record, whose premise 'crocodilians have four-chambered hearts' is a class rule (Decision 2). Here both premises are memberships about named taxa (the flea as plague's carrier, fleas in class Insecta), which admit no 'except' revision. Derivability likely: the class-level fact is almost never stated while both premises are; ratio of 'bubonic plague' near 'insect' (2.5%, sampled hits unrelated) to near 'fleas' (17.6%). Worlds: w1, fleas become arachnids (with what goes with that); w2, plague gets an arachnid carrier (e.g. a tick). Neither premise is entailed by other firm facts, so neither world is dropped. The combining rule is definitional and never gives way. The premise-route query asks the carrier's class through its description, as the template asks the time zone of 'the city the Space Needle stands in'. Legs are kept out of every query: fleas' six legs is a separate firm fact, and asking it would split w1 again (review lesson 2). R1: bubonic plague also spreads by direct contact with infected animals, but its only vector is the flea (insect); the direct prompt asks about biological classes explicitly. Same shape as biology-replace-0004 in the opposite direction (insect to arachnid). Verifier: 0003 and 0004 share the vector-to-class shape. No clean derived ABox alternative with individual-only premises was found: endemic-species chains (e.g. Darwin's finches in Ecuador) fail step 3 because the species' island is fixed by firm historical facts, so one premise cannot give way. Both are kept; they edit different facts in opposite directions. Formal check (FINDINGS B3): the 'insect or arachnid?' questions take for granted that bubonic plague has carriers of one class and that no animal is both; transmitted_by_class is many-valued in general (some diseases have vectors of both classes), so both are stated per record as bridges with checks. Since 2026-10-31 the one-class bridge, the paraphrase and the derived questions say 'arthropods', not 'animals': rats and other rodents are also said to spread plague, so 'animals of one class only' was false and 'Are the animals that transmit bubonic plague insects?' had a debatable 'yes'. Plague's arthropod vectors are fleas (and, on some accounts, lice), all insects.
